63:1: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: When the hypocrites come to you, O Muhammad, they will say with their tongues, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.’ And God knows that you are His Messenger. Whether the hypocrites said that or not, And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars. He says: God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars in their statement about themselves that they bear witness that you are the Messenger of God, because they do not believe that or have faith in it, so they are liars in their statement about themselves. Some Arab scholars used to say about His statement, And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars, that their conscience lied because they concealed hypocrisy. Just as their faith was not accepted, even though they had made it apparent, so too He made them liars, because they concealed something other than what they had made apparent.
63:2: God Almighty says: The hypocrites have taken their oaths as a shield, and they are their oaths. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, They took their oaths as a shield, meaning their oaths as a shield. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, They have taken their oaths as a cover, he said: They gather with it. He said: That is because they believed and then disbelieved. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, They have taken their oaths as a shield, meaning: Their oath by God that they are among you is a shield. His saying, Paradise: a screen in which they hide, just as someone hides in his garden in war and fighting, so they protect themselves, their children, and their money with it, and defend themselves from it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Paradise so that they may protect their blood and their wealth. His statement, So they turned away from the path of God, means: So they turned away from the religion of God with which He sent His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and His law that He legislated for His creation. Evil indeed was that which they were doing. These hypocrites who took their oaths as a shield, evil was that which they were doing in taking their oaths as a shield, because of their lying, hypocrisy, and other matters of theirs.
63:3: God Almighty says: Evil indeed is what these hypocrites did, who took their oaths as a shield because they believed in God and His Messenger, then disbelieved because of their doubt in that and their denial of it. His statement, Then He sealed their hearts, means: God placed a seal on their hearts of disbelief from faith. We have explained in a place other than this the nature of the seal on the heart with its evidence and the statements of the people of knowledge, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His statement, They do not understand, means that God Almighty says: They do not understand right from wrong and truth from falsehood, because God has sealed their hearts. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand. They acknowledged that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but their hearts were in denial and refused that.
63:4: The Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And when you see these hypocrites, O Muhammad, you will be amazed by their bodies because of the evenness of their creation and the beauty of their forms. And if they speak, you listen to their speech. The Almighty says: And if they speak, you hear their speech, their speech resembles the speech of people. And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars. He says that these hypocrites are as if they were propped up pieces of wood, with no good in them, no understanding, and no knowledge. They are only images without dreams and ghosts without minds. And His statement, They think that every shout is against them, means that God, the Most High, says: These hypocrites, due to their evil, bad opinion, and lack of faith, think that every shout is against them, because they fear that God will send down a command concerning them that will tear down their veils and disgrace them, and permit the believers to kill them, take their children captive, and seize their wealth. So out of their fear of that, whenever a revelation from God to His Messenger comes down to them, they think that it has come down with their destruction and ruin. God, the Most High, says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: They are the enemy, O Muhammad, so beware of them, for when they meet you, their tongues are with you but their hearts are against you, with your enemies, so they are the eyes of your enemies against you. And his saying, May God destroy them, how they are turning away from the truth, means: May God disgrace them, how they are diverted from the truth. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahib told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, and I heard him say about the statement of God, And when you see them, their bodies impress you, he said: These are the hypocrites. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa, except for Al-A’mash and Al-Kisa’i, read wood with a damma on the kha’ and the shin, as if they directed that to the plural of the plural. They pluralized the wood as khashban, then they pluralized the wood as khashban, just as they pluralized the fruit as fruits, then fruits. It may be possible that the wood with a damma on the kha’ and the shin is to be the plural of wood, so the shin is damma once and sukun another time, just as they pluralized the hill as akman and akman with a damma on the alif and the kaf once, and with a sukun on the kaf once, and as it was said: the body and the body, with a damma on the dal and a sukun on it for the plural of the body. Al-A’mash and Al-Kisa’i read that as wood with a damma on the kha’ and a sukun on the shin. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings and two eloquent languages, and whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. The sukoon in the middle is more common in the plural of fa’la as fa’l in nouns on the tongues of the Arabs, such as their plural of badana as badanan and ajma as ajman.
63:5: God Almighty says: And when it is said to these hypocrites: Come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he may ask forgiveness for you, they turn their heads, meaning they move them and shake them in mockery of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and of his asking forgiveness. And by stressing the waw of lawwa, the reciters read it as a report from them that they repeatedly shook and moved their heads and did so a lot, except for Nafi’, who read it with a light waw lawwa as if they did that only once. The correct reading in this regard is the one who stresses the waw, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on this. And His statement, And you saw them turning away, while they were arrogant, God Almighty says: And you saw them turning away from what they were called to, while they were arrogant, meaning: while they were arrogant about going to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask forgiveness for them. All of these verses, as mentioned, refer to Abdullah ibn Abi Salul, because he said to his companions, Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse, and he said, If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more humble. Zayd ibn Arqam heard of that and informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and asked him about what he had been told about, and he swore that he had not said it. It was said to him, “Why don’t you go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him to ask forgiveness for you?” So he began to turn his head and shake it in mockery, meaning that he would not do what they had advised him to do. So God Almighty revealed this surah about him from beginning to end. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, and the report came. Mention the narration that came with that: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, saying: Isra’il narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: I went out with my uncle on a military expedition, and I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Salul saying to his companions: Do not spend on those with the Messenger of God until they disperse. If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humble from it. He said: So I mentioned that to my uncle, and my uncle mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he sent for me and I told him. Then he sent to Abdullah Ali, may God be pleased with him, and his companions, and they swore that they had not said anything. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, denied me and believed him, and I was afflicted with a worry the like of which I had never experienced before. So I entered the house, and my uncle said to me: You did not want the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to deny you and hate you! He said: Until God Almighty revealed: When the hypocrites come to you. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for me, and he recited it, then he said: God Almighty has told you the truth, O Zayd. " Abu Kurayb and Al-Qasim bin Bishr bin Maruf narrated to us: Yahya bin Bakir narrated to us: Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hakam: I heard Muhammad bin Ka`b Al-Qurazi say: I heard Zayd bin Arqam say: When Abdullah bin Abi Salul said what he said: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse, and he said: If we return to Medina, he said: I heard him, so I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that, and some of the Ansar blamed me. He said: Then he came and swore that he had not said that, so I returned home and slept. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me, or it was reported to me, so I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, has confirmed you and excused you. He said: Then the verse was revealed: They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God.’ Abu Kurayb told us: Hashim Abu Al-Nadr told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, who said: I heard Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi say: I heard Zaid bin Arqam narrate this hadith. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated to us, saying: Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during a military expedition, and `Abdullah ibn Abi Salul said: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. `Abdullah ibn Ubayy swore that none of that had happened. My people blamed me and said: I did not intend this. So I went and slept sad or depressed. Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for me, or I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: God has accepted your excuse and confirmed your truth. Then this verse was revealed: “They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. ’” Until he reached: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us: Ibn Awn told me, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: Zayd ibn Arqam heard it and traced it back to his guardian. His guardian traced it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said to Zayd: Listen to me. Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ramadi told us: Ibrahim bin Al-Hakam bin Aban told us: My father told me: Bashir bin Muslim told me that it was said to Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul: O Abu Hubab, severe verses have been revealed concerning you, so go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that he may seek forgiveness for you. He turned his head and said: You ordered me to believe, and I believed. You ordered me to give the zakat of my wealth, and I gave it. So all that remains is for me to prostrate to Muhammad. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn aside. The whole verse he recited up to the wicked. It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy. That was because a young man from his relatives went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him a hadith about him and a serious matter. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him, and he swore an oath and disavowed that. The Ansar turned to that young man, and they blamed him and rebuked him. It was said to Abdullah, “Why don’t you go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?” He began to turn his head, meaning, You will not do it, and he lied about me. Then God revealed what you hear. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn their heads, Abdullah ibn Ubayy said, it was said to him, “Come, that the Messenger of God may God bless him and grant him peace may ask forgiveness for you,” so he turned his head and said, What did you say? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: His people said to him: Why don’t you go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he will ask forgiveness for you? So he began to shake his head, and the following verse was revealed about him: And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you.’
63:6: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “O Muhammad, it is the same for these hypocrites who were told, ‘Come, let the Messenger of God ask forgiveness for you,’ whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, God will never forgive them.” He says: God will not pardon them for their sins, but rather He will punish them for them. Indeed, God does not guide the wicked people. He says: God does not guide to faith the people who lie about Him, who disbelieve in Him, and who go against His obedience. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them - God will never forgive them. He said: This verse was revealed after the verse in Surat At-Tawbah, If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will never forgive them. (al-Tawbah 9:80), so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: More than seventy times. So God revealed, It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them - God will never forgive them.
63:7: God Almighty says, They are the ones who say, meaning the hypocrites who say to their companions, Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God, from among his emigrant companions, until they disperse, meaning: until they leave him. And His statement: To God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, meaning: To God belong everything in the heavens and the earth, and in His hand are the keys to the treasures of that. No one can give anyone anything except by His will. But the hypocrites do not understand, that this is the case, so they say: Do not spend on those with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they disperse. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. ’” He said: Do not feed Muhammad and his companions until famine strikes them, and they abandon their Prophet. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. ’” He recited it to the end of the verse. This is the saying of Abdullah bin Ubayy to his hypocritical companions: Do not spend on Muhammad and his companions until they call upon him, for if you were not spending on them, they would abandon him and leave him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse.’ Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said to his companions: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God, for if you did not spend on them, they would disperse. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse, meaning support and assistance, and not the obligatory zakat. Those who said this are the hypocrites. Al-Rabi’ bin Sulaiman narrated to us, saying: Asad bin Musa narrated to us, saying: Yahya bin Abi Za’idah narrated to us, saying: Al-A’mash narrated to us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, who said: When Ibn Abi said what he said, I informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he came and swore. The people began to say to me: Do you come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with lies? Until I sat in the house for fear that if they saw me they would say: This is the one who lies, until the verse, They are the ones who say was revealed.
63:8: God Almighty says: These hypocrites, whose characteristics He described before, say, If we return to the city, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. What is meant by more honorable is the more powerful and the more forceful. God Almighty said, To God belongs honor, meaning power and strength, and to His Messenger and to the believers in God, but the hypocrites do not know. It was mentioned that the reason for Abdullah bin Ubay saying that was because a man from the Muhajireen kicked a man from the Ansar. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Muammar told me, saying: Abu Amir told us, saying: Zama’ah told us, on the authority of Amr, saying: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: The Ansar were more numerous than the Muhajirun, then the Muhajirun increased in number and went out on a military expedition. A man from the Muhajirun kicked a man from the Ansar. There was a fight between them until he cried out: O group of Ansar, and the Muhajir cried out: O group of Muhajirun. report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: What do you have to do with the call of the Age of Ignorance? They said: A man from the Muhajirun kicked a man from the Ansar. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave it, for it is rotten. Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said: If we return to Madinah, the more honorable will expel the more humble from it. Umar said: O Messenger of God, let me kill him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not let the people think that the Messenger of God will kill his companions. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, They say, ‘If we return to Medina,’ to To God belongs honor and to His Messenger. He said: That was said by Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul Al-Ansari, the leader of the hypocrites, and some hypocrites with him. Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told me: Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam told us: My father told me on the authority of Ikrimah: “Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was called Hubab, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, named him Abdullah. He said: ‘O Messenger of God, my father is harming God and His Messenger, so leave me alone until I kill him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Do not kill your father, Abdullah!’ Then he came again and said: ‘O Messenger of God, my father is harming God and His Messenger, so leave me alone until I kill him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Do not kill your father!’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, perform ablution so that I may give him some of your ablution water to drink, perhaps his heart will soften.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution and gave him some. He took him to his father and gave him some to drink. Then he said to him: ‘Do you know what I gave you to drink?’ His father said: ‘Yes, you gave me your mother’s urine to drink.’ His son said: ‘No, by God, but I gave you to drink the ablution water of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.’” Ikrimah said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy was highly regarded among them, and this verse was revealed about al-Munafiqun 63:“They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. ’” He was the one who said, If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. He said: When they reached Medina, the city of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and those with him, his son took the sword and said to his father: “You claim, ‘If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. ’ By God, you will not enter it until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gives you permission.” Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, that a man from the Muhajireen kicked a man from the Ansar with his foot, and that was very bad for the people of Yemen. So the Muhajireen called out, O Muhajireen! and the Ansar called out, O Ansar! He said: The Muhajireen were more numerous at that time than the Ansar, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave it, for it is rotten. Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul said: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humble from it. Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me: Yahya bin Wasah told us: Ali bin Sulaiman told us: Abu Ishaq told us: Zaid bin Arqam told him that Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul said: Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. And he said: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more humble. Zaid told me that he informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what Abdullah bin Ubayy had said. He said: So he came and Abdullah bin Ubayy swore to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he had not said that. Abu Ishaq said: Zaid said to me: So I sat in my house until God revealed the confirmation of Zaid and the denial of Abdullah in When the hypocrites come to you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble, he recited the entire verse up to they do not know. He said: A hypocrite of great hypocrisy said it about two men who fought, one of them a Ghafari and the other a Juhani. The Ghafari gained the upper hand over the Juhani, and there was an alliance between Juhayna and the Ansar. A man from the hypocrites, Ibn Ubayy, said: O sons of Aws, O sons of Khazraj, your companion and ally is upon you! Then he said: By God, our example and that of Muhammad is like the saying of the one who said: Fatten your dog and it will eat you. By God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more humble. Some of them went to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Umar said: O Prophet of God, order Muadh ibn Jabal to strike off the head of this hypocrite. He said: Do not let people say that Muhammad kills his companions. He told us that he was sitting with a man of the hypocrites, so he said: Does he pray? He said: Yes, and there is no good in his prayer. He said: I have been forbidden from those who pray, I have been forbidden from those who pray. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Two men fought, one of them from Juhayna and the other from Ghifar. Juhayna was an ally of the Ansar, and the Ghifarite gained the upper hand over him. A man from among them, a great hypocrite, said: “Your companion is your enemy! You are your companion! By God, our example and that of Muhammad are like the saying of the one who said: ‘Feed your dog and it will eat you.’ By God, if we return to Madinah, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more humble.” While they were on a journey, a man who had heard them came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and told him what had happened. Umar said: Tell Muadh to have his head struck off. Muadh said: By God, people will not think that Muhammad kills his companions. Then the verse was revealed about them: They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God.’ And his saying: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more humble from it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, that a young boy came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I heard Abdullah ibn Ubayy say such and such. He said: Perhaps you became angry with him? He said: No, by God, I heard him say it. Perhaps you heard him wrong. He said: No, by God, O Prophet of God, I heard him say it. He said: Perhaps you misunderstood it? He said: No, by God. Then God revealed, confirming what the young boy had said: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took hold of the boy’s ear and said: Twist your ear, twist your ear, young boy. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, The more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble, he said: The hypocrites used to call the Muhajirun the cloaks. He said: Ibn Abi said: I have given you my command regarding these cloaks. He said: This is between Amj and Usfan at Al-Kadeed. They were disputing over water, and the Muhajirun had gained control over the water. He said: Ibn Abi also said: By God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. I told you: Do not spend on them. If you leave them alone, they will not find anything to eat, and they will leave and flee. So Umar ibn Al-Khattab came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, do you not hear what Ibn Abi is saying? He said: What is that? So he informed him and said: Let me strike off his head, O Messenger of God. He said: If many noses tremble for him in Yathrib. Umar said: If you do not like, O Messenger of God, for a man from the Muhajirun to kill him, then Sa`d ibn Mu`adh and Muhammad ibn Maslama passed by and killed him. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “I hate for people to say that Muhammad kills his companions. Call Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy for me.” So he called him and said: Don’t you see what your father is saying? The man said: And what is he saying, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you? The man said: He says, ‘If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more lowly.’ The man said: “By God, he has spoken the truth, O Messenger of God. By God, you are the more honorable and he is the more lowly. By God, I have come to Medina, O Messenger of God, and the people of Yathrib know that there is no one there who is more pious than me. If it pleases God and His Messenger that I bring them his head, I will bring it to them.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: No. So when they arrived in Medina, Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy stood at its gate with his sword for his father and said: Did you say, ‘If we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more lowly?’ By God, you will surely know that honor is yours or that of the Messenger of God. By God, his shade will not shelter you, and you will never shelter him except with the permission of God and His Messenger. He said: O Khazraj, my son is preventing me from my home. O Khazraj, my son is preventing me from my home. He said: By God, you will never shelter him except with his permission. So some men gathered around him and spoke to him. He said: By God, he will not enter it except with the permission of God and His Messenger. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: Go to him and tell him to leave him and his home. So they went to him. He said: If the command of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, comes, then fine. “Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah and Ali ibn Mujahid told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, and on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hayyan, who said: Each of them told me some of the hadith of Banu al-Mustaliq. They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed that Banu al-Mustaliq were gathering against him, and their leader was al-Harith ibn Abi Dhirar Abu Juwayriyah bint al-Harith, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of them, he went out to them until he met them at one of their watering places called al-Marisi`, on the side of Qudayd towards the coast. The people scrambled and fought, and God defeated Banu al-Mustaliq, and killed those of them who were killed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took their children, women and wealth, and God granted them booty. A man from Banu Kalb ibn Awf ibn Amir ibn Laith ibn Bakr, called Hisham ibn Subaba, was wounded. He was wounded by a man from the Ansar, from the people of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who thought he was from the enemy, and he killed him by mistake. While the people were at that watering place, a watering place came and…” Umar ibn al-Khattab had a servant from Banu Ghaffar called Juhajah ibn Sa`id who led his horse. Juhajah and Sinan al-Juhani, an ally of Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, clashed at the water and fought. Juhajah shouted, O group of Ansar! and Juhajah shouted, O group of Muhajireen! Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul became angry, and with him were some of his people, among them Zayd ibn Arqam, a young boy. He said, They did it? They have outnumbered us and outnumbered us in our country. By God, we have not returned to these cloaks of Quraysh except as the saying goes: Fatten your dog and it will eat you. By God, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel the more abject. Then he turned to those of his people who were present and said: “This is what you have done to yourselves. You have made them your country and shared your wealth with them. By God, if you had withheld from them what is in your hands, they would have moved to other countries.” Zayd ibn Arqam heard that and walked with him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished his campaign. He told him the report and Umar ibn al-Khattab was with him. He said: O Messenger of God, pass by Ubad ibn Bishr ibn Waqash and let him kill him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How will it be, O Umar, when people say that Muhammad kills his companions? No, but he gave permission to depart. This was at an hour when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not departing. So the people departed. Abdullah ibn Ubayy walked to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he heard that Zayd ibn Arqam had He heard what he heard from him, so he swore by God that he did not say what he said, nor did he speak about it. Abdullah ibn Ubayy was a noble and great man among his people. One of the companions of the Ansar who were present at the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, O Messenger of God, perhaps the boy is more mistaken in his speech and did not remember what the man said, out of concern for Abdullah ibn Ubayy and to protect him. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had departed and was on his way, Asid ibn Hudayr met him, greeted him with the greeting of the Prophet and sent him peace. Then he said, O Messenger of God, you have departed at an unusual time when you do not usually depart. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, Have you not heard what your companion said? He said, Which companion, O Messenger of God? He said, Abdullah ibn Ubayy. He said, And what did he say? He said: He claimed that if he returned to Medina, he would expel the most honorable from it. Asid said: By God, O Messenger of God, you can expel him if you wish. By God, he is the most honorable, and you are the most honorable. Then he said: O Messenger of God, be gentle with him, for by God, God brought you while his people were stringing beads for him to crown him, and he thinks that you have drawn him as a king. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked with the people that day until evening, and their night until morning, and the beginning of their day until the sun bothered them. Then the people dismounted, and it was not until they felt the touch of the ground that they fell asleep. He only did that to distract the people from the talk that had been the day before from the talk of Abdullah bin Ubayy. Then he went with the people and took the path of Hijaz until he dismounted at a spring in Hijaz above al-Naqi’, which is called Naq’a. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left, a strong wind blew on the people, bothering them and they were afraid of it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not be afraid, for it only blew for the death of a great one of the great disbelievers. When they arrived in Medina, they found Rifa’ah bin Zaid bin al-Tabut. One of the Banu Qaynuqa’, who was one of the great Jews and a refuge for the hypocrites, died that day. Then the surah was revealed in which God mentioned the hypocrites in Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and those who were with him in the same situation as him, saying: When the hypocrites come to you. When this surah was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took Zayd by the ear and said: This is the one whose ear God has fulfilled. And Abdullah bin Ubayy conveyed to those who were from his father.” “Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, that Abdullah ibn Ubayy came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have heard that you intend to kill Abdullah ibn Ubayy, as you have been told about him. If you are going to do it, then order me to do it, and I will bring you his head. By God, I know that there was no man among the Khazraj more dutiful to his father than me, and I fear that you will order someone other than me to kill him. My soul will not allow me to see the killer of Abdullah ibn Ubayy walking among the people and I kill him, killing a believer for an unbeliever and entering Hell. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, we will be gentle with him and treat him well as long as he remains with us. After that day, whenever he committed an act, it was his people who would rebuke him, seize him, scold him, and threaten him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar ibn al-Khattab when he heard about their behavior: What do you think, Umar? By God, if you had killed him the day you ordered me to kill him, my nose would have trembled if I ordered it today.” By killing his killers, he said: Omar said: By God, I know that the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more blessed than my matter.
63:9: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, Let not your wealth divert you meaning: Neither your wealth nor your children do not require you to be distracted from the remembrance of God, which is from diverted him from such and such, so he is distracted with it, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: And like you, a pregnant woman who has been knocked on the door and a nursing mother who has been distracted from the one who has amulets It was said: What is meant by the mention of God Almighty in this place is the five daily prayers. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. He said: The five daily prayers. His statement: And whoever does that means: And whoever is distracted by his wealth and children from the remembrance of God, then it is those who are the losers means: They are the ones who are cheated of their share of God’s honor and mercy, may He be blessed and exalted.
63:10: God Almighty says: And spend, O believers in God and His Messenger, from the wealth which We have provided for you before death approaches one of you and he says when death befalls him, O Lord, why would You not delay me and grant me respite in term until a near term? “So I would give charity” meaning: So I would purify my wealth “and be among the righteous” meaning: And work in Your obedience and perform Your obligations. It was said: What he meant by his saying and be among the righteous is that I perform Hajj to your Sacred House. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus and Sa`id ibn al-Rabi` told me. Sa`id said: Sufyan told us, and Yunus said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Janab, on the authority of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There is no one who dies without having paid the zakat of his wealth and without having performed Hajj, except that he asks for a return. They said: O Abu Abbas, you keep bringing us things that we do not know. He said: Then I will recite to you in the Book of God: And spend from what We have provided for you before death approaches one of you and he says, ‘My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term so I could give charity.’ He said: I would pay the zakat of my wealth and be among the righteous. He said: I would perform Hajj. Ibn Humayd narrated: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: What prevents one of you, if he has wealth on which zakat is due, from paying zakat, and if he is able to perform Hajj, from performing Hajj before death comes to him, and he asks his Lord for a return, but he is not given it? A man said: Do you not fear God? The believer asks for a return? He said: Yes, I will recite to you the Quran. Then he recited: O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. The man said: What makes Hajj obligatory for me? He said: A mount to carry him and the expenses to cover his expenses. Ibad bin Ya’qub Al-Asadi and Fadala bin Al-Fadl told us: Ibad told us: Yazid Abu Hazim, the client of Al-Dahhak, told us, and Fadala said: Buzay’ told us on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim regarding his statement, If only You would delay me for a short term so I could give charity, he said: So I could give charity from the zakat of my wealth, “and be among the righteous,” he said: Hajj. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God to the end of the Surah: He is the believing man upon whom death has befallen and who has a great deal of wealth which he has not paid zakat on, nor performed Hajj from, nor given from it what is due to God, and he asks to return at death so that he may pay zakat on his wealth. God says, And God will not delay a soul when its term has come. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God to His statement, And spend from what We have provided for you before death comes to one of you, he said: It is the believing man when death comes to him and he has wealth that he did not pay zakat on or perform Hajj from, and did not give God’s right in it, so he asks to return at death so that he can give charity from his wealth and pay zakat. God said, And God will not delay a soul when its term has come. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: So give charity and be among the righteous. He said: Zakat and Hajj. The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement, And I will be among the righteous. The majority of reciters of the regions, except Ibn Muhaisin and Abu Amr, recited it as And I will be in the subjunctive mood, based on the interpretation of his statement, So I will be truthful, if the fa was not in it. This is because his statement, So I will be truthful, if the fa was not in it, would be in the subjunctive mood. Ibn Muhaisin and Abu Amr recited it as And I will be by affirming the waw and placing And I will be in the accusative case, in apposition to his statement, So I will be truthful. So he placed his statement, And I will be in the subjunctive mood, since his statement, So I will be truthful was in the accusative case. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
63:11: And His statement, And God will not delay a soul when its term has come, means: God will not delay anyone’s term by extending it for him when his term has come, but He will shorten it. And God is Acquainted with what you do, means: God is All-Knowing of the deeds of His servants, He encompasses all of them, nothing is hidden from Him, and He will reward them for them, the good-doer for his good, and the evil-doer for his evil.
